notes.1: This question was generally well done. Many candidates scored all 4 marks. A number of candidates gave an answer of 5 which came from incorrect working. Answers: (i) 3N
notes.2i: Some candidates used the incorrect formula to find the centre of mass. A formula booklet is provided and should always be referred to. Too often the answer was left as 1/3π. Answers should be given to 3 significant figures. theirOG 0.25
notes.3: This question was generally well done.
notes.3i: Some candidates set up an energy equation to show that the KE when OP = 1.8 was zero. Having done that they failed to make the conclusion that v = 0.
notes.3iii: Quite often all marks were scored. Some candidates lost the final mark as no conclusion was made. Answers: (i) v = 0 (i.e. P is at instantaneous rest)
notes.3ii: P is on the point of losing contact with the surface.
notes.4: This question proved to be the easiest one on the paper. The majority of candidates scored all 6 marks.
notes.4iii: Distance from O when B hits the ground = 19.3m
notes.5i: The extension of 0.3m was often seen. Quite a number of candidates formed an energy equation with too many terms present.
notes.5iii: This part of the question was well done by many candidates. The use of F = μR was regularly applied. Answers: (i) Speed of P when B is first in limiting equilibrium = 1 ms–1
notes.6i: Too many candidates had incorrect distances in their moment equation.
notes.6ii: Tension in the string = 1.96N. Magnitude of the force exerted by P on the cone = 1.18N
notes.7i: a = 0.32ex was often found. On occasions a = –0.32e–x was seen. Using a = vdv/dx allowed the setting up of a differential equation. When solved this often resulted in the correct answer.
notes.7iii: From v = dx/dt = 0.8ex/2 another differential equation could be solved to find the required time. Some candidates used the rectilinear equations of motion. This was not permissible. Answers: (i) v = 0.8ex/2
notes.7ii: Time taken to travel 1.4m from O = 1.26s
notes.general_comments:
Generally the work submitted was neat and easy to follow.
Only a few candidates used g = 9.8 or 9.81 instead of g = 10.
